System description:
# Case: Tesla Model X with Autopilot (Mountain View, California, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-20/01. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2017 Tesla Model X has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings, vehicles and some objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, follows a vehicle ahead at a chosen gap, and returns to the set speed when no vehicle is ahead.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle in its lane using lane markings and the path of the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: steering torque is used to check that the driver's hands are on the wheel, with visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users and road workers share the highway. Road agencies maintain road markings and safety hardware such as barriers and crash attenuators.

## Operating context
Busy multi-lane freeway with high-occupancy-vehicle (HOV) lanes, exits and interchanges, lane markings of different quality, and traffic that changes in speed.

requirements.text: The system shall monitor driver engagement using steering torque, steering angle changes, and pedal inputs, and shall issue a visual and audible warning within 2 seconds if no driver input is detected for more than 5 seconds while Autopilot is active.
The system shall detect forward‑camera image quality degradation (e.g., glare) and, within 1 second, present a lane‑keeping unavailable alert and rely on radar/ultrasonic data for lane positioning.
The TACC shall increase the following gap proportionally when radar distance confidence falls below 80 % and shall not rely on measurements with confidence <80 %.

When an object is detected within the collision‑risk envelope, the forward‑collision warning shall be issued unless the object is classified as non‑hazardous with ≥95 % confidence; otherwise a warning shall be generated.
Autosteer shall initiate a corrective steering action when vehicle lateral offset reaches 30 % of lane width, ensuring the vehicle remains inside lane boundaries.
The user interface shall display a persistent notice that Autopilot does not detect temporary road‑work objects, and shall issue an audible/visual alert if cones or similar obstacles are identified.
When Autopilot is engaged, the power‑management module shall keep all ultrasonic sensors powered and shall raise a fault if any sensor is de‑energized.
If TACC does not receive an updated lead‑vehicle speed or distance command within 100 ms, it shall automatically reduce vehicle speed by at least 5 mph (or to a stop) and alert the driver.
The TACC controller shall inhibit any acceleration command when the estimated speed of the lead vehicle is ≤0 mph, maintaining current speed or decelerating instead.
VisionProcessing shall assess lane‑marking confidence; if confidence drops below 60 % for more than 2 seconds, Autosteer shall disengage and present a lane‑keeping unavailable alert.
